summary: Red team of the Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme extraction against arXiv v5 (hashes match; the published PDF is not served): fourteen findings, two high, six medium, six low. The items are faithful to the paper almost everywhere, and E1 holds. What breaks is ownership. (1) Route 3 sends the ∞-categorical K-theory the paper runs on (localizing invariants, S_• for stable ∞-categories, K^add, Land–Tamme, truncating invariants, the theorem of the heart, Thomason–Neeman, A-theory) to GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4/K.6/K.7. Those layers plan exact and Waldhausen K-theory, and their accepted blueprints are finished without it, so nothing plans the foundations the Part II imports. (2) Item /48 states Kuhn's theorem falsely: X^{tC_p} does not vanish for T(n)-local X; (KU_p^∧)^{tC_p} has π_0 = Q_p(ζ_p). (3) The chromatic basics were already routed by Clausen–Mathew 21, with an incompatible T(0) convention; that route was rejected, and the new chromatic roadmap is its natural owner. (4) ku, KU and Bott are planned at RT.4. (5) About a dozen cited theorems have no item, among them Waldhausen/LT Lemma 2.4, the Bousfield–Kuhn functor, Bousfield's theorem, the Hopkins–Smith theorems, BGT 9.53, Weibel's NK result and the Corollary 4.21 inputs. (6) /68's K_0 nil-invariance is not planned. (7) E2 is not a misprint in the printed paper. (8) The chromatic brief omits the Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology and ModularCurves owners. Low findings cover a Verdier-quotient double owner with NS18, two new misprints (Corollary 4.30 for 4.23; a stale CMNN numbering), item drift, Mathlib's 1-categorical Bousfield and t-structure API, /1's planned list, and provenance.

findings.claim: Route 3 sends the whole ∞-categorical K-theory apparatus the paper runs on to three layers that do not plan it, and those layers are now finished without it, so nothing in the atlas plans these twelve items. The items are: localizing invariants on Cat_∞^perf and K of a ring spectrum (/28); BGL(A)^+ for connective ring spectra (/29); the S_•-construction of a small stable ∞-category (/30); the Land–Tamme pullback theorem (/32); truncating invariants (/34); group-completion K-theory K^add (/40); the additive Schwede–Shipley theorem (/41); Thomason–Neeman localization (/43); the stable envelope (/55); Barwick's theorem of the heart (/56); Antieau–Gepner–Heller dévissage (/70); and Waldhausen A-theory (/76). (a) The stage texts are classical. K.4 is 'Define a Waldhausen category with zero object, cofibrations, weak equivalences …'. K.6 is 'One concrete route uses flasque enlargement and suspension …'. K.7 is Morita, products and filtered colimits. None mentions stable ∞-categories, Cat_∞^perf, localizing invariants, ring spectra or t-structures. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24.result.json: item /48 (Kuhn's blueshift theorem), statement; route 2 brief ('Kuhn's blueshift theorem for the Tate construction')
findings.claim: Item /48 states: 'For a T(n)-local spectrum X the Tate construction X^{tC_p} vanishes; consequently (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S'. The first clause is false, and it is the extraction's paraphrase, not the paper's. Kuhn's theorem says the Tate construction vanishes after T(n)-localization: L_{T(n)}(X^{tG}) = 0, equivalently the norm L_{T(n)}(X_{hG}) → X^{hG} is an equivalence for T(n)-local X. It also gives the blueshift form: X L_n^{p,f}-local implies X^{tC_p} L_{n−1}^{p,f}-local. It does not say that X^{tC_p} = 0. Counterexample: X = KU_p^∧ with trivial C_p-action is K(1)-local, hence T(1)-local (Mahowald–Miller). For a complex-oriented E with trivial action, π_*E^{tC_p} = E_*((x))/[p]_F(x). For KU_p^∧ the p-series is (1+x)^p − 1 = x·Φ_p(1+x), so π_0 = Z_p[[x]]/(Φ_p(1+x))[1/x] = Z_p[ζ_p][1/(ζ_p − 1)] = Q_p(ζ_p) ≠ 0. This Tate spectrum is rational, hence T(1)-acyclic, which is what Kuhn's theorem predicts; but it is not zero. The brief makes Kuhn's theorem a final theorem of ChromaticHomotopyTheory, so a design worker taking /48 as its formulation would plan a false target.
findings.evidence: Land–Mathew–Meier–Tamme, arXiv:2001.10425v5, Remark 3.9, p. 16: 'The spectrum (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is itself an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S by Kuhn's blueshift result [Kuh04]'. The paper states nothing stronger. Clausen–Mathew–Naumann–Noel, arXiv:2011.08233v2, p. 3: 'By Kuhn's "blueshift" theorem [Kuh04], if a spectrum X is L_n^{p,f}-local, then X^{tC_p} is L_{n−1}^{p,f}-local'. Same paper, p. 16: 'the composite map L_{T(i)}(M_{hG}) → M^G → M^{hG} is the norm, which is an equivalence since Tate constructions vanish in T(i)-local homotopy [Kuh04]'. The KU_p^∧ computation is given in the claim.
findings.fix: Restate /48 as: 'Kuhn [Kuh04]: for a finite group G and a spectrum X with G-action, L_{T(n)}(X^{tG}) = 0 (equivalently the norm L_{T(n)}(X_{hG}) → L_{T(n)}(X^{hG}) is an equivalence); in blueshift form, if X is L_n^{p,f}-local then X^{tC_p} is L_{n−1}^{p,f}-local, so (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S. The Tate construction itself need not vanish: (KU_p^∧)^{tC_p} has π_0 = Q_p(ζ_p).' Use this formulation in the route 2 brief.

findings.claim: The chromatic basics were already routed before this extraction, and neither the extraction nor its review noticed. PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 was merged on 22 September 2026, a day before this extraction. Its item /118, 'Chromatic localizations: L_1, L_{K(1)}, L_n^f, Morava K-theory and telescopes', and its items /150 (L_n^f-localized noncommutative motives), /024 (K(1)-acyclic connective spectra) and /142 (finite étale descent for L_n^f-localized K-theory, CMNN) all route to MotivicEtaleKTheoryPartIISelmerAndEtaleKTheory. REV-PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 then rejected that route precisely because 'generic chromatic/equivariant spectra … must be supplied by their owning roadmaps'. So when CM21 is revised, the ChromaticHomotopyTheory roadmap proposed here is the owner its revision needs, and neither brief says so. The two extractions also fix incompatible conventions. CM21/118 has 'T(0) = HQ' and 'L_n^f : Sp → Sp_(p) is p-localization followed by finite localization'. Here /16 has T(0) = S[1/p] and /20 has L_n^{p,f} = L_{T(0)⊕⋯⊕T(n)}. The CM21 item names only 'a telescope'; this item family fixes a pair (V_n, v_n). A single owner must adopt one convention and state the comparison. The report's search matched roadmap titles and layer text only; it did not look at the items other extractions route.

findings.claim: The paper's proofs cite about a dozen theorems that have no item, so they have no status, and several of them are also missing from both briefs. (a) The truncating properties of K(−)⊗S[1/p] on T(0)-acyclic ring spectra and of p-adic K-theory on S[1/p]-algebras (Waldhausen; [LT19, Lemma 2.4]). They are used in Proposition 3.1 (the T(0) part), Corollaries 4.4, 4.7, 4.16 and 4.23, and Remark 4.10; /31 only mentions them in passing. (b) The Bousfield–Kuhn functor, Φ_i∘Ω^∞ ≃ L_{T(i)} ([Kuh08, Theorem 1.1]). It is the whole proof of Proposition 2.9, but /25 states only the corollary. (c) Bousfield's theorem that highly connected spaces with trivial v_i-periodic homotopy are T(i)-acyclic ([Bou01, Corollary 4.8]; [BHM21, Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.3]), and the Serre spectral sequence in T(i)-homology, both used for Proposition 2.11. (d) Hopkins–Smith: the nilpotence theorem (Theorem 3), the thick subcategory theorem (Theorem 7), centrality of v_n self-maps (Theorem 11) and Corollary 3.8, all used in Lemmas 2.2(vii), 2.3 and 2.6. The brief names the first two; none is an item. (e) Mahowald–Sadofsky Proposition 3.3 and Lemma 2.1, used in Lemmas 2.6 and 2.2(vii). (f) [BGT, Theorem 9.53]: K_i(R) ≅ K_i(π_0R) for i ≤ 0 and R connective, used in Corollary 4.7. (g) Weibel: NK_*(A) is a Z[1/p]-module when p ∈ A^× [Wei81], the whole proof of Corollary 4.25. (h) The inputs of Corollary 4.21. These are: Ravenel's theorem that BP[v_n^{-1}] has the Bousfield class of K(0)⊕⋯⊕K(n) [Rav84, Theorem 2.1]; that complex-oriented rings of height ≤ n are L_n-local; that L_{n−1}-local spectra are T(n)-acyclic (which needs L_n smashing, Hopkins–Ravenel); and the lemma the proof proves in-line, that K(n)- and T(n)-localization agree on L_n-local spectra. They also include the GL_2(F_3)-Galois extension TMF_(2) → TMF(3)_(2) [MM15, Theorem 7.6], L_{K(2)}TMF(3) ≃ E_2, and Galois descent for telescopically localized K-theory [CMNN20, Theorems 5.6, Corollary B.4]. (i) The existence theorems behind /85 and /86: the E_∞-structure on Lubin–Tate E_n with its stabilizer action, and the sheaf O^top (Goerss–Hopkins–Miller, Lurie).
